title: Joining Lionel Hampton in San Francisco in 1942
summary: Cobb goes back to take up Hampton in order, recalling the Rum Boogie manager who called him and his phone talk with Hampton, who had heard him play Body and Soul in Houston.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Stanley, what did you ask me yesterday about Arnett? You said -- because we were talking about when we left off (inaudible) was still with (inaudible).
Yeah, we were going -- before we left off, you were going to Lionel Hampton.
Yeah, well, see, I joined Lionel Hampton in San Francisco at the Golden --
Have you got any other notes of old memories that you'd done before this?
No, the memories that I have here comes after the formation of my band and I got into mine, but we can go back to Lionel.
Let's go to Lionel now so we keep it in order.
Yeah. That's what I was wondering yesterday, if I'm jumping back and forth too much. Okay.

When I left the Rum Boogie, and I've told you about Ken Wood, who was the manager of the Regal Theater (inaudible), and Charlie Wood didn't like the idea that Ken was promoting me, which he wasn't. He just called me. And Charlie Wood didn't want to lose me directing the band. That's what the whole thing was.
But my wife and I -- in going to join Lionel, I talked to him at Ken Wood's office for 45 minutes from San
Francisco. He was in his first week, and he stayed there two weeks, and I joined him at almost end of the second week.
Well, I take it that Lionel, being in the room (inaudible), heard you.

He had. He had heard me in Houston. If you remember on your tape, I told you he asked me to play Body and Soul here at the El Dorado, and I just had gotten married. And if you ask a band leader to advance money for debts that you accrued, they won't give it to you, and I told him I was $500.00 in debt. Now, you've got it on the tape from yesterday.
